23. Room (f), wall N, section O: the stucco frame that concludes the upper area at the top, coeval with the painting of the IV style.
24. Room (f), N wall, section O: detail of the fluted pilaster with stucco ovoli cornices.

26. Room (f), wall N, section E: in the painting, of which only the band that frames it can now be distinguished, we must probably recognize the painting depicting Ganymede and the eagle (H, 156), already in a very poor state of preservation in the last century.

25. Room (f), N wall, section E, with stucco fluted pilaster. Fourth style decoration with plinth (black?) and middle area with central panel with a blue background, with vanished painting, and red side panels. The upper area is enclosed between two stucco frames.

27. Room (f), wall E with the row of windows with marble windowsills open on both sides of the viridarium (e). Remains of a fresco of the fourth style with a plinth (black?) and a middle area with red panels. You can see the stucco frames that delimit the middle area.

28. Room (f), wall S, section E with the door of (h) and rectangular window. Remains of a fresco of the fourth style with a black plinth and a red middle area, containing an evanid picture on the left; on the right the fluted pilaster covered with stucco that divides the room.
29. Room (f), S wall, section O: remains of a fresco of the fourth style with a painting in the center of the wall that is now illegible. The upper area is enclosed between two stucco frames.
30. Room (f), S wall, section O: the painting with Apollo and a female figure, now destroyed, is documented in this old photo taken in the last century.

31. Room (g), N wall with the door towards (h) surmounted by a low lunette. The decoration of the fourth style is of the simplest: above the low red plinth, the yellow middle area has panels bordered by carpet borders containing cartoons with animals, the upper area is white with architecture.
32. Room (g), N wall, section O: on the yellow of the panel of the middle area you can see the edges of the carpet and a volute in the center. IV style.
33. Room (g), wall E: low red plinth, yellow middle area with panels, upper white area with stucco architecture and cornice. IV style.

34. Room (g), S wall, with a square window open onto the Vicolo del Balcone pensile surmounted by a low stucco lunette, above which the housings of the floor beams can be recognized. Low red plinth, middle area with panels with carpet edges, upper white area with architecture. IV style.
35. Room (g), wall S, section O: the edges of the stapled carpet and the angular volute at the base of the panel can be recognized. IV style.
37. Room (g), O wall, section N: vignette with griffin flying to the right, in the red panel of the middle area. IV style.
36. Room (g), wall S, section O: the shadow of the vignette with a rampant animal on the right, depicted on the yellow background of the panel. IV style.

38. Room (h), N wall with the door opening onto the room (f), with marble threshold. The room, a small hallway protected by high walls, has preserved its decoration better than the surrounding rooms. Above the plinth with plants, the middle and upper areas are red: in the middle area we recognize at the bottom an edge of a carpet in semicircles, in the upper area the edges of a carpet with staples, a
39. Room (h), N wall, section O: upper red area with carpet borders, garland and swan in flight. IV style.
41. Room (h), S wall with the door of (g): remains of a fresco of the fourth style.
40. Room (h), wall E: remains of a fresco of the fourth style. In the lower plinth were depicted plants, the middle area, with edges of a carpet with staples, is red like the upper area.
43. Room (h), wall O, section S: red middle area with panel with staple carpet edges. IV style.
42. Room (h), wall O with the door leading to the work area (i): low plinth, red middle area with vignette and edges of a staple carpet, red upper area. 79 N52807
44. Room (h), O wall, section S: minimal traces of the vignette with a fantastic animal flying to the right are preserved. IV style.

45. Room (i): view from the N with the window open onto the Vicolo del Balcone pensile, above which the housings of the floor beams can be recognized. The walls of the work area are covered with a plinth of cocciopesto, above which the upper area is made of rough plaster.

46. Room (l), wall O: as we know from Mau (cited in the bibl.) the wall, restored with rough plaster, has a remains of the first style in the upper area, consisting of a red plane. Mau himself noted the peculiarity of this presence in a house in which no remains of older phases are preserved, underlining however that this wall (relic of a situation later abolished?) was in opus incerta of lava with a pillar in limestone blocks.
47. Room (1), N wall with the atrium door (b): remains of a fresco of the fourth style with a red plinth and a white middle area, preserved in the same state on the other three walls.
48. Room (m), wall E with square splayed window: on all the walls of the room there are illegible remains of frescoes.

49. Room (m), S wall, section W: in this remnant of a painting — of which only the engraved lines of the edge and some traces in the center can be recognized - (cf. the relief in Barbet, Allag MEFRA 19/72, fig. 56, with incorrect location in house no. 17-21) dobbiaINS. 12, 22-23-24
50. Room (o): wall with masonry bench and boiler and walls covered with cocciopesto plinth.
51. Cubicle (p), wall O, section S with recessed for the bed and tapped plaster for the superimposition of a second layer, collapsed.

1. Workshop (1) with entrance from no. 27, also accessible from the vestibule (a): N wall with a window open to the house, above which is a smaller, walled-in window; remains of a coating with high red plaster.

2. Workshop (1), wall E with the door communicating with the vestibule (a) of the house: the wall covering, of a functional nature, has a high red plinth that maintains the scansion in panels, while the upper area is in rough plaster.

3. Vestibule (a), wall E, to the S of the door communicating with the workshop with entrance at no. 25: on the high black plinth the red bands delimit the panels: the upper area had architecture on a white background. IV style.
4. Vestibule (a), wall W with the door communicating with the workshop at no. 27: remains of a fresco of the fourth style with a high black plinth and a white middle area.
5. Peristyle (c) with the wide door of the triclinium (h): the decoration of the IV style, which consisted of a black plinth and a red middle area, has completely collapsed.
7. Cubicle (d), wall N: the decoration of the fourth style, with a low plinth and a white middle area with a panel with a twisted candelabrum, is barely readable.

6. Peristyle (c), N portico, W wall, at the height of the triclinium (h): on the masonry in place on the frame, the decoration, completely collapsed, was concluded on the left by a semi-column covered with fluted white stucco, above which the tiles of the sloping canopy are visible in the masonry. Here was the lararium (Boyce, 321).
8. Cubicle (e), N wall with masonry in opus incerta with recourse of bricks, in which amphora bottoms are inserted; the plaster, illegible, is tapped for the superimposition of a second layer.

9. Triclinium (h): opus sectile floor inserted on three sides within a border of cocciopesto. From the careful analysis of Pernice (cited in the bibl.), who saw this floor in much better condition than the current ones, it appears that the front part (the one to which the remains reproduced here belong) was the original one, while the innermost part of the room, where the materials and shape of the tiles changed, dated back to a readaptation of the original floor. The latter has a motif attested in the Republican age and also present in the oecus of the Villa of the Mysteries: the squares — here of gray marble — bordered by red strips. The threshold with alternating hexagonal tiles

10. Triclinium (h), wall N. The old photograph is the only evidence that allows us to evaluate the decoration of the room, now almost completely vanished. The middle area has in the center an aedicule with wings in perspective on a yellow background, within which is a painting depicting Ariadne abandoned; in the red side panels are medallions. In the center of the upper area, with architecture, a statue of Ares can be recognized (H, 272). IV style.

12. Triclinium (h), N wall, section O: in the red panel of the middle area there is a medallion with the bust of a girl holding a stylus and diptych (H, 1423), legible only in the old photograph and now completely lost. IV style. FU7251F

13. Triclinium (h), N wall, central section: painting with the abandonment of Ariadne by Theseus (H, 1231). The girl wakes up on the beach of Naxos, where she is represented in the company of winged Nemesis, on the left, who shows her the boat of Theseus moving away, and a cupid who wipes his tears by lowering his (useless) bow. In the lower right corner are two personifications that allude to the marine setting of the story.

14. Triclinium (h), N wall, section E: on the red background of the middle area, the medallion, pendants of the one reproduced in fig. 12, represents a bust of a child with a scroll (H, 1420 b), completely vanished. IV style.

15. In the drawing of N. The Fox (cfr. Draftsmen, p. 717, fig. 181) are reproduced, in addition to the medallion of the previous figure, the female portrait in fig. 12, the medallion with Satyr playing the syringe (H, 423) from wall E, section N and the one with Paris and cupid (H, 1275) in fig. 20.

16. Triclinium (h), wall E, section N: red plinth with panels separated by narrow compartments with plants; middle area with central aedicule with yellow background with removed painting and red side panel with medallion, separated by architectural foreshortening; upper area with stucco architecture and cornice. IV style.

17. Unlike the painting with Ariadne abandoned, left in situ without adequate protection and now completely destroyed, the painting with the sale of cupids from wall E (H, 823) has undoubtedly been detached due to the rarity of the subject and is now in the Museum of Naples (inv. 111437). E interes574

19. Triclinium (h), wall O, section S: the red plinth has panels with carpet edges separated by narrow compartments with plants; in the middle area, within the red panels de-mitated by carpet edges, are the medallions with busts, separated by architectural views; in the upper area there are remains of a structure with aedicules. IV style.
18. 'Triclinium (h), wall E, section S with the door of (i): remains of a fresco of the IV style with a medallion in the centre of the red panel.

20. Triclinium (h), wall E, section S: on the red panel of the middle area we can only recognize the outlines, engraved with the compass, of the medallion containing a bust of Paris with cupid (H, 1275), the iconography of which we can see in the drawing reproduced in fig. 15. The same subject appears in the triclinium (c) of the house
21. Triclinium (h), wall O, section S: the illegible remains of a medallion with bust, executed within circles engraved with a compass. IV style.
22. Triclinium (h), wall W, section S: medallion with bust of a girl (H, 1421d) in the red panel of the middle area. IV style. 79 N51848
23. Triclinium (h), O wall, S section: the vanished traces of the architectural foreshortening of the middle area. IV style.

24. Triclinium (h), W wall, central section. The wide red plinth panel is flanked by two compartments with plants; in the aedicule (?) with a yellow background in the middle area is the large hole left by the detachment of the painting with Artemis and Kallistò, on the sides of which the architectural views and the red side panel can be recognized; the upper area, which contained architecture, ends with the molded stucco frame. IV style.

25. Triclinium (h), wall O, central section: red panel of the plinth, with flower within a rhombus, framed by rectangular carpet borders and a stretched garland; on the yellow background of the middle area you can see the edges of the carpet in semicircles. IV style.

26. The painting with Artemis and Kallistò (H, 253), detached from the section of the wall reproduced in fig. 24, now in the Museum of Naples, (inv. 111441). The same subject is present in the adjacent house, VII 12, 28 (cf. p. 611, fig. 34) and, in an iconographically concordant version, in the triclinium of the House of the Tragic Poet (cf. vol. IV, p. 581, fig. 102), already mentioned several times (the same subject in House IX 5, 6: Schefold W, p.54; Herrmann-Bruckmann 1906, p. 28, tav. 19; for the interpretation of the scene cf. E. Simon, in LIMC, II, p. 838, n. 342 X, s.v. Artemis/Diana, with incorrect location; I. Mc Phee, in LIMC, V, p. 943, n. 15, s.v. Kallisto). The painting is certainly the work of the same hand to which we owe the one with cupids' nest. Diap. AFSN 11414
27. Triclinium (h): the NW corner preserves the remains of the stucco frame with lotuses and palmettes.

28. Area (i), wall O: the uncovered area onto which the rooms (k), (m) and (n) open and a secondary door of the triclinium (h) also has a wall covering of the fourth style, of which only the partitions can be recognized: the discolored plinth, the red middle area, with panels bordered by carpet edges separated by compartments containing candelabra,  the upper area with stucco architecture and cornice.  79 N62446
29. Area (i), wall O, section N: stucco frame with lotuses and palmettes. IV style.
30. Room (k): cocciopesto floor in which square tiles were inserted (subsequently?), in marble like the threshold.
32. Room (k), N wall, central section: white compartment with twisted candelabrum. IV style.

31. Room (k), wall N: above the red plinth, the scheme is divided into two parts by a central white compartment, closed by a red partition and crossed by a twisted candelabrum; the side panels are yellow, bordered by square carpet borders, and contain medallions. Above the moulded frame in
33. Room (k), N wall, section O: medallion with bust of cupid. IV style.
34. Room (k), N wall, section E: medallion with bust. IV style.
35. Room (k), wall E: remains of a fresco of the fourth style: red plinth, middle area with central compartment and yellow side panels; stucco frame. IV style.

36. Room (k), O-shaped wall of the door of (l): red plinth with carpet edge panel with two parallel lines; yellow middle area with panel with rectangled carpet edges. The decoration of the IV style is in continuation of that of area (i).

37. Room (k), S-shaped wall of the door of (1): above the wall reproduced in fig. remains, of the stucco frame and holes in the grappas that supported the protruding part; in the upper white area it is still possible to recognize the edges of the carpet with triangles and two parallel lines: on the latter rests a pecking bird, above which is
38. Room (k), wall O to N of the door of (1): red geometric plinth, yellow middle area with carpet edge panel. IV style.

39. Room (k), wall O, section N: detail of the red geometric plinth, with medallion and edges of carpet with two parallel lines. IV style. The circle engraved with the compass (you can still recognize the hole left in the center by the rod) is not framed within the guide lines drawn vertically.
40. Room (1), wall W with lunette: remains of an illegible fresco, preserved in the same state on the other three walls. 79 N51889

41. Room (m), wall N: the decoration of the fourth style, although extremely poor, shows a partition between antechamber and alcove obtained by means of a thin pilaster. Above the plinth — red-paneled with plants — the middle area is yellow-paneled; the upper area, white, has carpet edges in the antechamber, and a medallion between stretched garlands in the alcove. The stucco frame is molded.

42. Room (m), N wall, central section: detail of the pilaster separating the antechamber and the alcove, schematically decorated with V-shaped motifs, enclosed within fields that reproduce the mirrored partition of the pilasters decorated with greater commitment. IV style.

43. Room (m), wall E with lunette: the decoration of the alcove, with a symmetrical scheme, has above the red plinth the yellow middle area with a central aedicule and side panels with carpet edges; in the upper area the motif of the stretched garland present in the adjacent section of the N wall continues. Above the lunette, in the left corner, a section of the original roof can be recognized. The decoration of the fourth style, now completely lost, was very simple and included vignettes in the panels and in the aedicule, one of which depicted a mermaid with fedum (Fiorelli, p. 127, no. 249; Fiorelli D, p. 291).

44. Room (m), wall E, section S: edges of a carpet with two parallel lines and a wreath stretched in the upper area. The motifs are hardly recognizable, due to the degradation of the colors. IV style.
45. Room (m), S wall with square window with marble sill open onto area (i): fresco of the fourth style with a red plinth with plants and a yellow paneled middle area.

46 Room (m), wall W, antechamber: red plinth with plants; yellow middle area with central aedicule and side panels with carpet edges with two parallel lines; yellow dentilled frame; White upper area with stretched garlands and carpet edges. This wall retains in better condition the decoration of the fourth style, to be counted among the simplest of this scheme, with the only enrichment being the central aedicule, which contained a vignette with cupid (cf. So 271 and 310).
47. Room (n), wall E with masonry in opus uncertain with recourse of bricks, covered with illegible remains.

48. Room (0), N wall with the window with a marble sill that takes light from the peristyle (b), onto which the door also opens. The decoration of the fourth style, miserably collapsed (the black plinth and the middle area with yellow and red panels with carpet edges can be recognized) and preserved in the same state on the E and S walls, contained a series of figurative elements of which only the reproductions made at the time of the excavation remain; of a painting with Maenad and bust of Satyr we have only the news of Helbig (H, 512).

49. Room (W), wall W: above the plinth you can recognize in the middle area the shadow of the central panel on the red background of the panel, to the side of which there are narrow compartments and yellow panels. IV style.

50. N.'s drawing The Fox (cfr. Disegnatori, p.718, fig. 182) preserves the iconography of the small picture with Heracles and Omphales (H, 1032), which was part of the fourth style decoration of the room (0).
51. Painting with Satyr and Maenad (H, 551), which was part of the lost decoration of the room (0) (reproduction by N.La Volpe; cf. Disegnatori, p. 719, fig. 183).

52. Painting with a female figure with a casket pedume (H, 1526b), lost and preserved only in this reproduction contemporary with the excavation (cf. Disegnatori, p. 720, fig. 184: N. La Volpe). This painting was also part of the decoration of the room (0). ADS 748 (Fot. Pedicini)
1. Vestibule (a): the floor in the papier-mâché has been broken by the insertion of the lead fistula. 79 N51968
2. Vestibule (a), wall N, jamb O: pilaster. with a red plinth and a coating of white grooved stucco in the upper area, against which the viridarium column (G) leans.
3. Vestibule (a), wall E, section N: in the red panel of the middle area there is a golden candelabrum. IV style.

4. Vestibule (a), wall O with the door preceded by three steps of the room (c): to the left of the staircase the wall covering is functional, with a high red plinth surmounted by the white middle area; in the innermost section, on the other hand (in the foreground of the photo), pertaining to the house, the plinth and red middle area had a decorative scheme of the fourth style, now lost.

6. Room (d), N wall, section O, with window with marble sill open onto the viridarium (g). The red plinth has the common ornamentation consisting of panels alternating with compartments with plants; in the red middle area you can recognize an edge of a triangle carpet. IV style.
5. Room (b), NW corner: the wall cladding consists of a high plinth and a white middle area, in which no ornamentation can be recognized.
8. Room (d), wall W with the door open to the vestibule (a) and remains of fresco of the IV style.
7. Room (d), wall E, section N: decoration of the fourth style with a bipartite structure on a red background.

9. Room (e), wall N: also in this room the decoration of the fourth style is of the simplest and has plants in the compartments and panels of the red plinth. The middle area is yellow, and alternates panels with carpet edges with narrow compartments crossed by twisted candelabra.
10. Room (e), N wall, section O: detail of the upper area (with a red background?) in which light architecture with garlands can hardly be seen. IV style.
11. Room (e), N wall, section O: compartment with plants of the red plinth. IV style.
12. Room (e), wall N, section O: the stucco frame with lotuses and palmettes that concludes the upper area of the IV style.

13. Room (e), S wall: remains of a fresco of the fourth style with a red plinth, in which panels and compartments with plants alternate; yellow middle area with panels with carpet edges separated by compartments with candelabras; Upper yellow area with architecture. The fresco has been completely preserved, up to the height of the stucco frame, but the degradation of the surface layer of color allows only the skeleton of the simple decoration to be read.
14. Room (e), wall O: remains of fresco of the fourth style. In the center of the middle area was a medallion of which only the contours engraved in the plaster can be distinguished.

15. Atrium (f), corner N-0 with the door of the room (1): the decoration is lost on all the walls, but Helbig (H, 1585) places in this room a farddeisos, a decoration consisting of a landscape populated by wild beasts which, more frequent in viridaria, highlights the mixed function of this part of the house.

16. Atrium (f): in correspondence with the fountain of the viridarium (g) is a marble table with trapezophores beaked with lion's paws, ending at the top with heads crowned with leaves, datable to the imperial age.
17. Atrium (f): detail of one of the marble trapezoids, ending with heads crowned with leaves.

19. Viridarium (g): in the center of the room, and in axis with the view of the room (k), is a low marble basin within which a rectangular marble basin rests on a fluted travertine support, probably older. The water of the fountain behind poured into this basin, consisting of a statuette of a child holding a shell in his left hand, from which the water flowed (cf. Zanker P79, p. 203, fig. 110), now removed. The original layout of this fountain can be obtained from the
18. Viridarium (g), wall E, with lava drainage channel and cylindrical dolii: on the wall — as on the other walls of the room — the cladding is illegible.
20. Viridarium (g): the lead fistula with bronze taps that feeds the fountain reproduced in the previous figure.

21. Room (h), N wall with remains of a fresco of the fourth style: in the red plinth there are panels with plants; the yellow middle area has panels with triangle carpet edges; in the upper area (red ?) you can recognize a garland and a band with triangle carpet edges. IV style.

22. Room (h), S wall, with remains of frescoes of the IV style that also cover the holes of the beams of the attic. The red plinth has panels with plants; the yellow middle area is divided into two parts by a compartment with a candelabra, on the sides of which are panels with carpet edges; the upper area is red (?).
23. Room (h), W wall with two niches (one of which is walled up) and remains of a fresco of the fourth style.

24. Room (i), wall N: the decoration is more preserved in this room, but it is also of a mediocre level as (despite the presence of a number of figurative motifs) in the rest of the house. The central panel of the plinth is red, with garlands within the edges of the carpet, and the side compartments with hanging drinking horns are also red; in the yellow side panels are plants. The middle area, with a yellow background, has a newsstand in the center flanked by architectural views; The side panels — depicted in half on each wall — are yellow with a high red border and contain cartoons with animals. IV style. 79 N52038
25. Room (i), wall N, section O: the simplicity of the decoration of the room is also evidenced by the ornamental motif of the panels, the vignette with animals (here it is a swan). IV style.
26. Room (i), N wall, section E: red compartment with rhytòn hanging in the plinth. IV style.
27. Room (i), wall E, section N: remains of a fresco of the fourth style.
28. Room (i), S wall: the fresco of the fourth style is much more damaged here than on the wall in front, in fig. 24. 79 N51959
29. Room (i), wall W with fresco of the fourth style. 79 N51985
30. Room (i), wall O, central section: vase at the base of the panel and partition with mask that closes the side view. IV style.

31. Room (k), wall N: the fourth style decoration of the room included a series of paintings: Silenus with Dionysus as a child (H, 374); on this wall there was a fragment with a "cupid's nest", a subject present — like Artemis and Kallistò on wall E — also in House VII 12, 26, as well as a series of vignettes with Seasons (H, 976, 992 and 1003); Nothing remains of all this except the background colors: red the plinth and the plinth, yellow the middle area. In this room there was also the floor with the emblem of opus sectile of colored marble.

32. Room (k): emblem of opus sectile of colored marbles, with a black and white mosaic border, inserted within a floor of cocciopesto with ornamentation of white tesserae, described by Blake and Pernice (cit. in the bibliography).

33. The remains in situ of the painting with the 'cupid's nest', recognizable because the part preserved in this old photograph is directly comparable with the other three Pompeian replicas of the same subject (cf. p. 576, fig. 17, House VII 12, 26, by L. Cornelius Diadumenus; cf. Micheli 1992, pp. 2-14). Sogliano (So 143) vi
34. Room (k), wall E: here was the fragmentary painting with Artemis and Kallistò (H, 255), a subject also present in the adjacent house at no. 26 (cf. p. 580, fig. 26) as well as

35. Room (k), wall O: the small canopy was certainly not able to protect the painting (H, 1161) in which the story of Admetus and Alcestis is recognized, in an iconography attested by a certain number of paintings from the period of the fourth style (including the one from the House of the Tragic Poet, cf. vol. IV,  pp. 546547, fig. 36; cf. also M. Schmidt, in LIMC, I, p. 541, Kb, s.v. Alkestis), which autonomously compose a series of elements freely drawn from the literary tradition.
36. Room (k), wall O, section S: aedicule with picture with dolphins. IV style.
37. Room (k), W wall, N section: red plinth with narrow compartment with bird. IV style.
38. Room (k), wall O, section N: panel with lozenge and edges of a triangle carpet in the red plinth. IV style. 79 N51976
40. Apotheca (n), N wall with holes for wooden shelves and wall covering divided between a high plinth and a middle area. 79 N51986
39. Area (1), wall E with the imprint of a wooden staircase, which led to the room above the apotheca (n), with an attic supported by wooden beams of which the recesses can be distinguished.

2. Environment (2) with entrance also from no. 25; wall N, section O: in the masonry in opus incerta there is a drainage channel from the upper floor, composed of clay elements. The wall — against which a jamb of tiles leans — is covered with frescoes, now illegible.

1. Room (1), wall W, with masonry in opus quadrata of tuff blocks and in opus incerta (which preserves the traces of the closure of a window), covered with a fresco covering that is now illegible. 79 N55212
3. Room (2), wall E with remains of an illegible fresco. On the N wall — in which a window opens — there is a masonry counter.

1. The shop, accessible from the entrance at no. 3, communicates with the atrium of the house through the door that can be glimpsed on the left of the photo. The shop was initially larger and also included the one adjacent to no. 2, which was later detached from the property and made independent. The jamb of the façade, open onto Via dell'Abbondanza in the immediate vicinity of the Forum, is made of large blocks of tuff; the wall E, in uncertain work, preserves the holes for the beams of the floor at the top and has an illegible coating. 79 N55211

2. Vestibule (a'), floor: very little is preserved of the chopped cocciopesto, in which flakes of colored limestone are densely scattered, a type of flooring that finds comparisons in houses of the Republican age.

4. Room (e), S wall, section E: on this side the oldest fresco, of the fourth style (black plinth, red middle area with edges of a triangle carpet, yellow upper area), is better distinguished, against which the opus mixtum pillar is leaning with the remains of a fresco with a black background (plinth and middle area).

3. Room (e), wall S, section to the E of the door; Pillar in opus mixtum of tuffs and bricks, leaning against the tuff block masonry: on the latter you can still recognize the black plinth and the yellow middle and upper areas. The leaning pillar is also frescoed in the fourth style: the plinth is purple; the middle yellow area with a narrow panel adorned with a vignette depicting a horse in flight.

5. Room (e), S wall, section O, redecorated in the last phase with a purple plinth and a yellow middle area, in which the architectural foreshortening and the side panel with a carpet border can be distinguished. IV style.

6. Room (e), wall O: purple plinth with a central panel with garland and candelabra, on the side of which there is a narrow compartment and another panel; in the middle yellow area in the center is a shrine, in the side panel a vignette with a doe and edges of carpet in semicircles. IV style.

1. The Rooster fountain is one of only two marble fountains in Pompeii, which had 43 public fountains. It was built partly on the sidewalk and partly on the roadway of the road that took its name from it, and which thus remained forbidden to wagons. Because of this peculiarity and because of its proximity to the entrance of the house, it was believed that the owner of the Sailor's House may have built it. It rests, for the part protruding from the sidewalk, on a block of lava probably belonging to a previous fountain, in which a canal was dug to convey waste water to the street. The monolithic blocks are held in connection by large metal clamps, while the cannola made of bronze is lost, due to the casting that came out of the upper plate.
